conflicts.fact: Nakuru mast height / angle used in the anchoring problem
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 give 50° with 40 m, so h ≈ 47.7 m. Lesson 5 says the mast problem is re-solved with 60° as 40 tan 60° = 40√3 ≈ 69.3 m, presented as the 'exact height of the Nakuru Kenya Power mast', which conflicts with the 50° scenario.

conflicts.fact: Angle of depression from the mast top equals the angle of elevation (alternate angles) vs complementary angle
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 claims the angle of depression from the top of the mast is 40° (complement of 50°) and that either angle gives the same height. Lesson 7 teaches that elevation from A to B equals depression from B to A, so the depression would be 50°, not 40°.

conflicts.fact: Dhow/boat problem values (Fort Jesus depression problem)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7's Observed says the dhow distance ≈ 28.6 m (teacher demonstration) and later the Mombasa dhow ≈ 31.1 m (group problem). Lesson 8 uses a different Lake Victoria problem with 120 m, elevation 38°, depression 22°, whereas the overview of the same lesson says depression 32° and elevation 25°.

conflicts.fact: Lake Victoria lighthouse problem angles within Lesson 8
conflicts.versions: Overview: fisherman on a cliff sees the boat at depression 32° and the boat sees the lighthouse at elevation 25°. Explain phase: boat 120 m away sees the lighthouse at elevation 38° and the coastguard sees the boat at depression 22°.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson established the complementary-angle rule and where trig tables were first made
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says sin 30° = cos 60° confirms the complementary-angle rule from Lesson 4 and uses 'trig tables from Lesson 3'. In the sequence the complementary rule is Lesson 3 and tables first appear in Lesson 2; Lesson 4 is the tan identity. Lesson 5 also says 'Our rule from Lesson 1: sin θ = O/H', but the formal definitions were in Lesson 2.

conflicts.fact: Source of the data table used in Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says learners use the Lesson 2 table of sin, cos, tan for 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°. Lesson 2 has learners measure triangles at about 35° and 60° and look up their angles; Lesson 3's table uses pairs 20/70, 25/65, 30/60, 35/55, 42/48, 15/75 with sine and cosine only.

conflicts.fact: Mast geometry: where the hypotenuse/angle sits
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 gives sin 40° = cos 50° = 0.6428 as the 'mast-problem pair' (sin 40° is actually 0.6428 and cos 50° is 0.6428, which is consistent), but says the model labels 'sin 50° = cos 40° = h/hypotenuse', i.e. 50° as elevation, while Lesson 1 identifies tan 50°=O/A as the core ratio; it is fine, but Lesson 3 includes a 'hawk' depression at 40°, inconsistent with Lesson 7's rule.

conflicts.fact: Kisumu ramp problem answer and the tan 50° value
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 gives tan 50° ≈ 1.1918, ramp hypotenuse ≈ 6.13 m; Lessons 2 and others use tan 50° ≈ 1.192 (consistent rounding). Lesson 6 Predict has Kisumu ramp as a find-the-ramp-length problem with 6 m horizontal, but Observed describes cos 12° = 6/hypotenuse, consistent. Lesson 6's Predict problem C mast in Garissa says it 'makes a right angle with the ground' but is 45 m tall with wire anchored 45 m away, whereas Explain Problem 3 gives a Garissa tower with a 32 m shadow and 62° elevation.
